title: The Free Gift Card
intro: An email says a two-minute survey earns you a gift card. Easy money, it seems.
Tap anything that looks odd to sniff it closer. Pin what is suspicious, clear what is harmless.
When you are sure, decide what to do.

notify.text: Take our survey and get a €100 gift card

subject.text: Take our 2-minute survey: win a €100 gift card!

p: to give us your opinion. It takes only two minutes.
from a store of your choice.

addr.label: A strange address
addr.lens: The email comes from free-gift-surveys.com, which is not any store you shop at.
addr.why: Look at the part after the @. It should match a company you know.

greet.label: "Dear Valued Customer"
greet.why: A vague greeting alone proves little, but it fits mass mailings.

picked.label: "You were selected"
picked.lens: You never signed up for anything.
picked.why: Being picked out of nowhere is a warning sign.

prize.label: €100 for two minutes
prize.lens: A big reward for a tiny task.
prize.why: Big pay for little work is the bait.

link.label: Look-alike link
link.lens: The button goes to a survey page that is not the store's own site.
link.why: Never start from a link in an unexpected email.

card.label: Asks for your card
card.lens: A "free" gift card that wants your card number for €1.99.
card.why: A reward that wants your card is a trap.

from.label: Friendly name
from.lens: The sender is called Customer Rewards.
from.why: A name is easy to copy.

actions.label: Click Start and do the survey
Check the store's own site for any survey

trap.title: Rewards survey
trap.ask: Answer three questions, then enter your card number for €1.99 delivery.

block_report.line: Reported as phishing and deleted. The fake address was blocked within days.

verify.line: The store's own site had no survey and a warning about fake gift-card emails. Case cracked.

ignore.line: You stayed safe. But the same scam is still landing on other people.

go_ahead.line: The "delivery" page copied your card details. No gift card came, and strange charges did.

what_if.go_ahead: A reward that asks for your card number is never a reward.
what_if.ignore: Reporting takes two taps and helps protect other people.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting it as well helps protect other people.

golden_rule: A free gift card that wants your card number is a trap. Real rewards never need your card.

quick_check.q: An email offers a €100 gift card for a survey, then asks for your card number for €1.99 delivery. What do you do?

options.text: Fill the survey but skip the card
Delete it, and report it as phishing

quick_check.explain: A reward that wants your card is the trap. Even starting on the page is risky.

hints.nudge: Why would a free gift card need your card?

rows.v: a page that asks for your card
